brief: John Keble was born in 1792. He was concerned for the future of the Church of England and pleaded for the restoration of ancient Catholic liturgical practice, devotional life, and doctrine. He was an early leader of the Oxford Movement. His sermon on “National Apostasy” in 1833 criticised the church for allowing ten Irish bishoprics to be dissolved by Parliament. He defended the apostolic autonomy of the church against liberal tendencies, which he regarded as corrupting. He was known for his humility and spiritual insight. He died in 1866.
